clause.quote: The presence of a genus/version count code that appears as the first element within the framed material of any non-overrideable count code (universal or not) MUST have no special meaning as an override to the stream parser.
clause.section: Universal Code table genus/version codes that allow genus/version override

inferred_from.inference: A genus/version code that opens a non-overrideable group is read as whatever the group's framed material is, so where that material must be indexed signatures or primitives, a parser should reject the group rather than switch tables and skip the code.
inferred_from.quote: The presence of a genus/version count code that appears as the first element within the framed material of any non-overrideable count code (universal or not) MUST have no special meaning as an override to the stream parser.
inferred_from.section: Universal Code table genus/version codes that allow genus/version override

description: After a KERI 2.0 inception, an attachments group holds a -K whose framed material is the genus/version code -_AAACAA followed by one indexed signature, with -K's size counting both. -K is not one of the codes that allow a genus/version override, so the code has no override meaning there (line 816), and a -K's framed material is indexed signatures, which -_AAACAA is not. A parser that treated the code as an override would skip it and accept the group, as it must inside -C (CESR-0029). The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.
title: Reject a controller signature group whose first element is a genus/version code
